data.name: Auto_Installing
data.comment: {0} is a comma-separated list of what is being installed and {1} the environment it is going into.

data.name: Auto_RefusedOptions
data.value: Not installed: {0}. A dependency has to name a package; these are installer options, which a notebook is not allowed to pass. Remove them, or run the install yourself with #!pip if you meant them.
data.comment: Entries in the Dependencies setting that were skipped. {0} is a comma-separated list of them.

data.name: Auto_RefusedSources
data.value: Not installed: {0}. A dependency has to name a package; these name somewhere to install from, which would have fetched code from a location the notebook chose rather than from the configured index. Name the package instead, or run the install yourself with #!pip if you meant them.
data.comment: Entries in the Dependencies setting that were skipped for pointing somewhere else. {0} is a comma-separated list of them.

data.name: Auto_UnknownDistribution
data.value: '{0}' is not installed and Verso does not know which distribution provides it. Automatic installs only cover known packages; install it with #!pip {0} if that is the right name.
data.comment: A cell imported something Verso cannot map to a package. {0} is the name the cell imported, and appears twice.

data.name: Consent_Source_DeclaredDependency
data.comment: Why the consent dialog is asking: the notebook lists this package among the ones it needs. Appears beside the package name, in brackets.

data.name: Consent_Source_Import
data.comment: Why the consent dialog is asking, quoting the line of Python that needs the package. `import` is a Python keyword and stays as written; {0} is the module name.

data.name: Install_AlreadyInstalled_One
data.comment: Nothing was done. {0} is one package name with its version.

data.name: Install_AlreadyInstalled_Other
data.comment: The same for more than one. {0} is a comma-separated list.

data.name: Install_AlreadyPresent
data.comment: Names what was there before the install. {0} is a comma-separated list with versions.

data.name: Install_Completed
data.comment: The install worked but said nothing this could read, and nothing was asked for by name.

data.name: Install_Dependencies
data.comment: Names what came along with the request. {0} is a comma-separated list with versions.

data.name: Install_DependencyCount_One
data.comment: How many packages came along with what was asked for, written for exactly one.

data.name: Install_DependencyCount_Other
data.comment: The same for any other number.

data.name: Install_ExitedWithCode
data.comment: The installer ran and gave up. {0} is the number it exited with.

data.name: Install_Installed
data.comment: {0} is a list of packages with their versions, or a count already written out.

data.name: Install_InstalledAnd
data.comment: {0} is what was asked for, {1} a count of what came along with it, already written out.

data.name: Install_NothingToDo
data.comment: The install ran and added nothing, because it was all there.

data.name: Install_PackageCount_One
data.comment: How many packages were installed, written for exactly one. Goes into the sentence above.

data.name: Install_PackageCount_Other
data.comment: The same for any other number.

data.name: Install_Packages
data.comment: Names what was installed when none of it matches what was asked for by name.

data.name: Install_RunFailed
data.value: Failed to run the package installer: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the underlying error, which arrives in English.

data.name: Install_StartFailed
data.value: Failed to start the package installer.
data.comment: The installer would not run at all.

data.name: InterpreterSource_CondaPrefix
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: a conda environment. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_DerivedEnvironment
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: an environment Verso made for this notebook. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_Explicit
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: chosen in the settings. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_Path
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: found by looking along the system's search path. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_SessionSelection
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: chosen with #!python earlier in this session. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_VirtualEnv
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: the virtual environment that is currently active. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_WellKnown
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: found where an installer usually puts one. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: InterpreterSource_WorkspaceVenv
data.comment: Where an interpreter came from, shown in brackets after it in a list: a virtual environment inside the open folder. Keep it to a word or two.

data.name: Kernel_Description
data.value: Python language kernel running the interpreter installed on this machine.
data.comment: What the Python kernel is, shown wherever kernels are listed.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Description
data.value: Installs Python packages via pip for use in subsequent code.
data.comment: What #!pip does, shown in the list of magic commands.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Installing
data.comment: Printed before the install starts, so a slow one does not look like nothing happening. {0} is a comma-separated list of package names.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Name
data.comment: Name of the #!pip magic command as an extension, as listed in the Extensions panel. The command word itself is typed into a cell and is not translated.

data.name: Magic_Pip_NoInterpreter
data.value: No Python interpreter is available, so there is nothing to install into. Install Python 3.8 or newer, or select an interpreter with #!python.
data.comment: Packages need somewhere to go, and there is no Python on this machine that Verso can use.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Param_Options
data.value: Additional pip options passed through to the install command.
data.comment: What the second argument to #!pip is.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Param_Packages
data.value: One or more package specifiers (e.g. pandas==2.0 numpy).
data.comment: What the first argument to #!pip is. The two package names are examples and stay as written.

data.name: Magic_Pip_Usage
data.comment: Shown when #!pip is given nothing to install. Everything after 'Usage:' is typed at a keyboard and stays as written.

data.name: Magic_Python_Active
data.comment: What #!python prints with no argument. {0} is the path, {1} the version, {2} the implementation name such as CPython, and {3} the kind of environment. The last two stay as they are reported.

data.name: Magic_Python_Description
data.value: Inspects or selects the Python interpreter for the current session.
data.comment: What #!python does, shown in the list of magic commands.

data.name: Magic_Python_DiscoveredHeading
data.comment: Heading above the list #!python --list prints. Each interpreter follows on its own line.

data.name: Magic_Python_ExternallyManaged
data.value: This interpreter is externally managed; installs use a Verso-managed environment.
data.comment: Added to the end of the message above. It opens with a line break because it is a line of its own.

data.name: Magic_Python_Name
data.comment: Name of the #!python magic command as an extension, as listed in the Extensions panel. The command word itself is typed into a cell and is not translated.

data.name: Magic_Python_NoneFound
data.comment: Nothing on this machine looks like a Python that Verso can use.

data.name: Magic_Python_NotFoundFor
data.value: No Python interpreter was found for '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the path, name, or version number that was asked for.

data.name: Magic_Python_Param_Target
data.value: A path or name to select, or --list to show discovered interpreters. Omit to show the active interpreter.
data.comment: What the argument to #!python is. --list is typed at a keyboard and stays as written.

data.name: Magic_Python_RestartFailed
data.value: The kernel could not be restarted automatically ({0}). Run #!restart to apply the selection.
data.comment: {0} is the underlying error, which arrives in English.

data.name: Magic_Python_Selected
data.comment: The first half of a sentence finished by one of the two below. It ends in a space because the rest follows on the same line. {0} is the path to the interpreter and {1} its version.

data.name: Magic_Python_SelectedAppliesLater
data.value: It applies the next time the Python kernel starts.
data.comment: Finishes the sentence above when no kernel is running to restart.

data.name: Magic_Python_SelectedRestarting
data.value: Restarting the kernel to apply it.
data.comment: Finishes the sentence above when a kernel is running and is being restarted.

data.name: Setting_Dependencies_Description
data.value: Requirement strings installed into the notebook's Python environment before the first cell runs, under the same consent policy as an import. One per entry, in the form pip accepts (for example "pandas>=2"). An entry has to name a package: installer options and locations such as a URL, a version control reference or a path are refused, because a notebook does not choose where packages come from.
data.comment: What the setting above does, shown under its name. The example in quotation marks is typed at a keyboard and stays as written.

data.name: Setting_Dependencies_Label
data.comment: Name of a setting, shown in the settings panel. Keep it short; it sits on one line above a list.

data.name: Setting_HideInstallOutput_Description
data.value: Report an install as the packages it added and the versions they came in at, rather than relaying everything the installer printed on the way there. Installing one package pulls in its dependencies, and the resulting screen of text is saved into the notebook alongside the output the cell was actually run for. An install that fails is always reported in full.
data.comment: What the setting above does, shown under its name.

data.name: Setting_HideInstallOutput_Label
data.comment: Name of a setting. Keep it short; it sits on one line beside a switch.
